notes: Grounded in pipeline/validation/report.md's 'deep-balance-2026-07-28 / Checkpoint A (BEFORE)' block: kitted D2-D9 measured 93.5-98.5 percent (provisional targets 70-84), finale 85.0 percent measured against a 48 target with 120 of 170 finale wins (70.6 percent) closing round 1. That kitted profile (dev/kitted-profile.ts) already carries hotBoot and longArms in BOOST_SCHEDULE and jamAnchor/siphonPlus/tripwire in MODE_PAIRS, so every buff to those five in this batch moves numbers arc-composer and validation are already tracking; hotBoot and echoTap are filed as tone-down CANDIDATES for that reason; land them only after a Checkpoint B re-measure with this whole batch applied, not as an isolated delta. echoTap itself is not in BOOST_SCHEDULE or MODE_PAIRS today, so this cycle's kitted sim cannot confirm or deny its S-tier read at all; recommend the Orchestrator add it as a fourth MODE_PAIRS slot (or swap it in for tripwire on the armHalt/lock pair for a comparison run) before trusting any before/after number on it specifically. Cuts cite the user's tier list (surge C, bulwark D, carryCache F, slagWard F). Pool math: 18 shipped entries today (4 config, 14 boost); this batch cuts 4 boosts and adds 4 boosts, netting 18 total (4 config, 14 boost) after integration, unchanged and still comfortably under the ~20-boost dilution line. Directions considered and NOT selected for the four replacement boosts, so a future cycle does not re-propose them cold: POUCH EXTENSION (+2 pouch cap, requires pouch) was dropped as too similar in shape to SPLICE REFUND below (both onboard the same new pouch system; picking both would have been two cards doing one job) and CLEAN PAY BENDER (flat plus 15cr on any at-or-under-par win) was dropped in favor of buffing CLEAN RUN's own capped-fire case instead of adding a second, near-duplicate par-win payout augment alongside it. OVERTIME CLAUSE and DARKNET RATE were selected in part because the brief's own scope list names the overtime-clause tone flag as something the loremaster gates this cycle, and the darknet framing is this cycle's headline new fiction surface, so both need a mechanical anchor in the catalog to gate against.

Remove the AUGMENTS entry and that one conditional line. Orphans nothing.

items.name: OVERTIME CLAUSE
items.desc: Cap wins pay 75 percent of the ticket instead of 50. The client eats every hour past the deadline, not half.
items.synergy: Pairs with CLAMP DRIVER (cfgLock) and WARD DRIVER (cfgWard) stall builds: PAR's rotation budget already makes forcing opponent reroutes profitable on its own (per the story-retune-1 diagnosis in agent memory), so a build content to grind to ROUND_CAP on purpose stops eating the same penalty as a build that blunders into the cap by accident.
items.counter: The turn-cap tiebreak in endOppTurn still hands the win to whichever side's routeCost is lower at the cap, so OVERTIME CLAUSE pays nothing if you are not also closer to the core than the opponent; this cycle's flat gridlock strain chip and the existing PAR_STRAIN_PER overage bill still apply in full on a cap win, so a clean core win stays strictly better paid regardless.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook, run layer only, no duel-layer change. run-reducer.ts's jobPayFor(run, capWin) currently returns `capWin ? Math.floor(pay / 2) : pay`. Change the capWin branch to `capWin ? Math.floor(pay * (run.kit.augments.includes("overtimeClause") ? 0.75 : 0.5)) : pay`. jobPayFor already receives `run`, so `run.kit.augments` is in scope with no signature change. Tone flag: carries a loremaster gate per the brief's scope list (the 'overtime billing' framing needs to read as the shop's own economy, not exploitative labor framing, before its copy ships).

items.name: DARKNET RATE
items.desc: Dark web patch piece pulls cost 15 percent less. The vendor still only takes credits and the roll stays blind.
items.synergy: Stacks with a heavy darknet-buy strategy instead of drop or craft reliance: cheaper pulls let a player who whiffs the shape odds (PATCH_ROLL_WEIGHTS I 40, L 45, T 12, X 3 in patch-cells.ts) reroll more times per night's credits, complementing CLEAN RUN and post-dive drops rather than replacing them.
items.counter: The discount only ever touches darkPatchCost(day), which already climbs with day under this cycle's economy retune (25 plus 5 times day minus 1); it narrows the sink, it does not remove it, and the roll stays random, so a discounted pull can still hand back a shape the pouch has no use for yet.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook. patch-cells.ts already exports the pure `darkPatchCost(day)` helper this cycle. The darknet-buy dispatch itself (the night-shop action that actually spends credits for a roll) is not on disk yet; it is part of this cycle's own Orchestrator engine work (WS1, per the brief). Wherever that dispatch lands, it needs to price through `Math.round(darkPatchCost(day) * (run.kit.augments.includes("darkDiscount") ? 0.85 : 1))` rather than calling `darkPatchCost` directly. Flagging honestly: this is a hook into code that does not exist yet, not a retune of a shipped call site.

items.name: SPLICE REFUND
items.desc: Placing a patch piece refunds its 1 RAM the instant it lands. The pouch still spends the piece itself.
items.synergy: Pairs with the LONG ARMS reach buff below (reach 4 lets a placement land further out for the same free cast) and with CLEAN RUN's own piece payout: pieces earned by playing clean cost nothing to actually use, so a par-clean build spends its stockpile freely instead of hoarding it for one emergency rescue.
items.counter: Refunds the RAM, never the piece: the pouch (PATCH_POUCH_MAX = 5, patch-cells.ts) still drops by one per placement, so this cannot chain into free placements without pieces already in hand; a fresh junction opened this way is still unwarded, so an opponent's armHalt or armSiphon punishes it exactly as hard as an unrefunded placement, since SLAG WARD is retired this same batch.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook. duel-actions.ts applyPlace, right after `econ.ram -= 1;`: add, when `side === "player" && kitHas(s, "patchRefund")`, `econ.ram += 1;`. This is the exact call site SLAG WARD's rider used (a few lines earlier in the same function, both keyed off kitHas inside applyPlace), so it is a like-for-like hook swap. Draft gating: requires {kind:"pouch"} needs rollDraft (run-reducer.ts) to drop this id from `remaining` until the run has actually held a patch piece (e.g. `run.patchCells > 0` ever true, or the equivalent non-empty check once the pouch becomes an array of PatchMask this cycle), before the configs-guaranteed-slot logic runs, so a dead card never fills the guaranteed or a random slot. ENGINE-PASSIVE: qualifies for dev/kitted-profile.ts's BOOST_SCHEDULE. The kitted policy bot already places cells autonomously (per Checkpoint A's per-day note: 'places a cell when it is a rescue, a shortcut of 2+ rotation RAM, or the placement that makes this turn the closing turn'), so this refund needs no new bot logic, only the reducer hook above.

items.name: FIRST FAULT
items.desc: The first trap that fires on you each dive bills zero Neural Strain. Every trap after that costs full.
items.synergy: Pairs with SCAN and PURGE builds still catching up their scan tier: a scan then purge combo that lands one cast too late no longer bricks a clean-win attempt outright, and it lets a CLAMP DRIVER or WARD DRIVER build risk one exploratory rotation into unscanned territory per dive without eating the strain tax for it.
items.counter: Only the STRAIN bill is forgiven, never the tempo: a halt trap still forfeits the whole turn (loseNextTurn) and a siphon trap still drains RAM at the shared SIPHON_STEAL rate on the very first trap same as any other, and the forgiveness is spent the moment any trap fires, including one planted deep in territory SCAN never reached, so a build leaning on this still wants SCAN tier or TAP LINE to make the forgiven hit a cheap one rather than a costly one.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook, one line. duel-actions.ts finishDuel, the win branch: currently `chip += 4 * s.econ.player.trapsFired;`. Change to `chip += 4 * Math.max(0, s.econ.player.trapsFired - (kitHas(s, "firstFault") ? 1 : 0));`. No new state; s.econ.player.trapsFired is already counted per fired trap inside settleFloods. ENGINE-PASSIVE: qualifies for dev/kitted-profile.ts's BOOST_SCHEDULE. Pure state-based strain math with no bot decision required, so it applies automatically to whatever trapsFired count the kitted bot already produces on any day.

items.name: JAM ANCHOR
items.desc: Your REDIRECT also freezes the junction it twists through the opponent's next reply and into your own following turn. Nothing rotates or redirects it back while it holds.
items.synergy: REDIRECT's unlimited reach (redirectTargetLegal carries no reach check, unlike plain rotation) plus a freeze that now actually survives into your next turn turns a single cast into real board control at any distance; stacks with cheapShot's free first ATTACK for an opening jam that costs nothing.
items.counter: A node the target already self-locked or warded is untouchable by REDIRECT at all, existing legality checks deny the cast outright, so this does nothing against a defender already running CLAMP DRIVER or WARD DRIVER on that spot.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook. duel-actions.ts applyCast's redirect branch currently sets `c.lockedThroughRound = Math.max(c.lockedThroughRound, s.round);` when kitHas(s, "jamAnchor"). Because lockedThroughRound is compared `>= s.round` and s.round only increments once per full round (in endOppTurn, after the opponent's reply), that write expires the instant the round increments, meaning the freeze only ever survives the opponent's immediate reply and never reaches the player's next turn, weaker than the current copy implies. Change the write to `s.round + 1`. Must be simmed together with the halt package below (tripwire, cfgArmHalt HOLD) since both touch lockedThroughRound-adjacent timing this batch, even though jamAnchor rides REDIRECT and tripwire rides ARM HALT.

items.name: LONG ARMS
items.desc: Rotate open junctions up to 4 steps from your territory instead of 2. Bigger setups, bigger cascades, and it stretches how far a patch piece can be placed too.
items.synergy: Pairs with SPLICE REFUND above (a free-RAM placement now reaches further out) and the buffed TAP LINE (a 2-round trace survives long enough to plan a 4-step chain before it goes stale).
items.counter: Reach without claims: an opponent's REDIRECT (also unlimited range) can untwist a distant setup for the same 1 RAM it cost to line it up, and a chain 4 steps out sits exposed to any armHalt or armSiphon planted along the way for that many more turns before it ever claims anything.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook. duel-power.ts reachOf currently returns `BASE_REACH + 1` (3) when the player owns longArms. Change to `BASE_REACH + 2` (4). canPlace(s, side, idx) calls reachOf(s, side) directly for patch-piece placement legality, so this reach buff extends to where a piece may be placed as well as where a node may be rotated; no separate hook needed for that half. Checkpoint A's kitted profile already schedules longArms at day 4 in BOOST_SCHEDULE, so this number is already load-bearing on the measured D4-D9 overshoot (all +21.5 to +39.0 over provisional target); re-measure at Checkpoint B with the rest of this batch, not in isolation.

items.name: SIPHON DRIVER
items.desc: ATTACK config: plant siphon traps. A sprung trap drains RAM from its next turn into yours, more at higher ATTACK tiers, and more again when you are the one springing it.
items.synergy: DEEP SIPHON (siphonPlus, now gated behind owning this config, see its own requires update below) stacks its own plus 1 on top of the new player-side baseline, and ECHO TAP's RAM reward compounds off a siphon trap that already bites harder than the shared table alone suggests.
items.counter: PURGE and the buffed SWEEP CREDIT strip an armed siphon before it ever fires; WARD DRIVER denies the plant outright in its zone. The baseline bonus is read off `side`, not a new augment, so the opponent's own siphon traps never get it: the shared SIPHON_STEAL table itself stays untouched and identical for both sides, per this cycle's rule against retuning shared tables.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook, NOT a change to the shared SIPHON_STEAL table (kit.ts, must stay identical for both sides this cycle). duel-actions.ts applyCast, the arm branch's drain calc for kind === "siphon" currently: `drain = SIPHON_STEAL[tierOf(s, side, "attack")] + (side === "player" && kitHas(s, "siphonPlus") ? 1 : 0);`. Add a player-only baseline ahead of the siphonPlus term: `drain = SIPHON_STEAL[tierOf(s, side, "attack")] + (side === "player" ? 1 : 0) + (side === "player" && kitHas(s, "siphonPlus") ? 1 : 0);`. This reads off `side`, so it applies to every player running the config, buffing ARM SIPHON itself rather than gating the buff behind a second draft pick. Checkpoint A's kitted profile cycles the armSiphon/purge/siphonPlus pair in MODE_PAIRS from day 3, so this is also load-bearing on the measured overshoot; re-measure with the batch.

items.name: DEEP SIPHON
items.desc: Your siphon traps steal 1 extra RAM.
items.synergy: cfgArmSiphon's new player-side baseline above; stacks additively on the same drain calculation.
items.counter: PURGE and WARD DRIVER, unchanged.
items.engineNote: Draft-gating only, no numeric change. Add `requires: {kind:"augment", id:"cfgArmSiphon"}` so rollDraft (run-reducer.ts) never offers a plus-1-siphon-drain boost to a kit that cannot cast ARM SIPHON at all yet, the same dead-card problem tripwire's own requires fixes below. Needs a small rollDraft filter, before the configs-guaranteed-slot logic runs: drop any augment from `remaining` whose `requires.kind === "augment"` and `!ownsAugment(run.kit, requires.id)`.

items.name: TRIPWIRE
items.desc: Your halt traps also burn 3 RAM off the victim's next active turn.
items.synergy: Stacks with the JAM ANCHOR duration buff above and with HALT DRIVER itself: a target that eats a lost turn from ARM HALT and then a 3 RAM burn the turn after is looking at two damaged cycles in a row. Simulate the whole halt package, HALT DRIVER (HOLD), JAM ANCHOR's new duration, and this bump, together, not as three independent deltas.
items.counter: SCAN then PURGE, unchanged; WARD DRIVER denies the plant outright.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook, plus a draft-gating add. duel-actions.ts applyCast's arm branch: `else if (side === "player" && kitHas(s, "tripwire")) { drain = 2; }` becomes `drain = 3;`. The bump is meant to close a real gap: the burn is a RAM drain scheduled the round AFTER the halt trap's own lost-turn effect resolves (settleFloods sets `econ.drainNext += trap.drain` on the side that sprung it, consumed at that side's NEXT beginTurnEconomy, itself the turn after the forfeited one), so it reads as a bigger hit than it delivers. Also add `requires: {kind:"augment", id:"cfgArmHalt"}` per the same rollDraft filter as siphonPlus above, so this is never offered to a kit that cannot cast ARM HALT. Checkpoint A's kitted profile schedules tripwire on the armHalt/lock MODE_PAIRS entry from day 3; re-measure with the whole batch.

items.name: TAP LINE
items.desc: SCAN also traces the intrusion's planned route to the core, visible for 2 rounds instead of 1.
items.synergy: Pairs with LONG ARMS and SPLICE REFUND above: a 2-round trace survives long enough to plan a multi-rotation chain or a far placement before it goes stale, instead of expiring the instant your own turn ends.
items.counter: The trace is a snapshot of routePlan at cast time; it does not update as the opponent reroutes around your own LOCK or WARD, so a trace one round old can already be wrong about where they are actually headed.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook. duel-actions.ts applyCast's scan branch sets `s.routeTrace = { round: s.round, cells: ... }`; endOppTurn clears it with `if (s.routeTrace && s.routeTrace.round < s.round) s.routeTrace = null;` after incrementing s.round, which today drops the trace the instant the cast round ends (it survives only the same round it was cast in, not a full round as the old copy implied). Change the stored value to `round: s.round + 1`; no change to the clear check itself.

items.name: SWEEP CREDIT
items.desc: PURGE refunds 1 RAM per trap it defuses, up to 3 RAM per cast.
items.synergy: Makes SCAN into PURGE a sharper counter to arming: a max-width purge that lands clean now nets a real profit instead of merely breaking even, restoring the halt or siphon versus scan or purge triangle without touching either trap's own numbers.
items.counter: Traps planted outside your SCAN_RANGE stay invisible to a player caster (purgeTargetLegal requires trap.revealed), so an opponent that scouts your scan tier and plants past it dodges the refund entirely; a purge cast that clears nothing still costs the full RAM regardless of the cap.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook. duel-actions.ts applyCast's purge branch currently: `if (n > 0 && side === "player" && kitHas(s, "sweepCredit")) { econ.ram += PROGRAM_COST; }` (flat refund regardless of how many of the `n` traps cleared). Change to `if (side === "player" && kitHas(s, "sweepCredit") && n > 0) { econ.ram += Math.min(n, 3) * PROGRAM_COST; }`. The cap of 3 matches DEFEND_WIDTH's own tier-3 ceiling (kit.ts), so a max-width purge that lands clean refunds its full cost plus 2 extra RAM, never more.

items.name: CLEAN RUN
items.desc: Win a dive at or under par with no traps sprung, and bank a patch piece. A trap-free win that only misses because it ran to the round cap pays 15 credits instead.
items.synergy: Pairs with OVERTIME CLAUSE above: a build that grinds to the cap on purpose (CLAMP DRIVER or WARD DRIVER stall) no longer walks away from an otherwise trap-free game with nothing extra, since `kind === "cap"` always adds 10 to chip in finishDuel, so the existing chip-zero condition can never fire on a cap win even when zero traps fired.
items.counter: Still denied entirely by a single sprung trap, same as the piece payout; the 15cr consolation is flat regardless of how close to par the cap win ran, so it never outpays a genuine chip-zero piece grant on a build that can reliably close under par instead.
items.engineNote: New reducer hook alongside the existing one. run-reducer.ts's duelFinished, next to the existing `cleanRunFired = action.chip === 0 && run.kit.augments.includes("cleanRun")` line: add `const cleanRunCapBonus = !cleanRunFired && action.capWin && action.trapsFired === 0 && run.kit.augments.includes("cleanRun") ? 15 : 0;` and fold it into pay: `const pay = ticketPay + salvage + cleanRunCapBonus;`. `action.capWin` and `action.trapsFired` are already carried on the duelFinished action (RunAction union); no duel-layer change needed.

items.name: WARD DRIVER
items.desc: DEFEND config: ward an area so no new traps can land in it, and REDIRECT cannot touch anything inside it either, for the full duration on both sides.
items.synergy: WARD_RADIUS tier scaling (kit.ts, unchanged): a tier 3 ward now holds its full duration for the caster too, closing the one place WARD was actually weaker for the player than for the machine.
items.counter: CLAMP DRIVER still wins head to head on a single chokepoint since it also freezes plain rotation, which WARD never touches; a caster willing to spend two ATTACK casts can bait the ward with one redirect and land the real one after it lapses.
items.engineNote: Retune of an existing hook. duel-actions.ts applyCast's ward branch currently: `const through = side === "player" ? s.round + WARD_ROUNDS - 1 : s.round + WARD_ROUNDS;`. Drop the asymmetry: `const through = s.round + WARD_ROUNDS;` for both sides. WARD_ROUNDS itself (kit.ts) is untouched and shared, unmodified per this cycle's rule against retuning shared tables; only the player-side offset in this one call site changes.

items.name: HOT BOOT
items.desc: CANDIDATE, sim-gated, not applied this batch. Would change to: start every dive with +1 RAM on your first turn (was +2).
items.synergy: Unchanged: pairs with cheapShot for a free opening ATTACK plus extra tempo.
items.counter: Unchanged: the opponent's own ramPerTurn (day config, oppRam) is untouched, so this only ever closes part of an early tempo gap, less of it if tuned down.
items.engineNote: Candidate retune, sim-gated: NOT applied automatically in this batch. duel-setup.ts, `s.econ.player.ram = playerRamPerTurn + (kit.augments.includes("hotBoot") ? 2 : 0);` would become `... ? 1 : 0`. hotBoot is dev/kitted-profile.ts's BOOST_SCHEDULE day-2 slot, meaning EVERY kitted seed carries it from day 2 onward, so this single number moves the whole kitted curve, not just the mode it touches. Checkpoint A measured D2-D9 kitted at 93.5-98.5 percent against 70-84 percent provisional targets. Land the tone-down only after re-measuring with the boost-bay cap, shaped pieces, and this batch's other buffs already in place, so it is not double-counted against changes the other agents are landing the same cycle.

items.name: ECHO TAP
items.desc: CANDIDATE, sim-gated, not applied this batch. Would change to: whenever one of your traps fires, gain 1 RAM on your next turn (was 2).
items.synergy: Unchanged: rewards any trap-heavy build regardless of attack mode.
items.counter: Unchanged: only fires off a trap the opponent actually walks into, so a WARD-heavy opponent denies it outright.
items.engineNote: Candidate retune, sim-gated: NOT applied automatically in this batch. duel-actions.ts settleFloods: `if (otherSide(side) === "player" && kitHas(s, "echoTap")) { s.econ.player.drainNext -= 2; }` would become `-= 1;`. Flagging a measurement gap honestly: echoTap is NOT referenced in dev/kitted-profile.ts's BOOST_SCHEDULE or MODE_PAIRS today (only hotBoot/longArms and jamAnchor/siphonPlus/tripwire are), so this cycle's kitted sim cannot confirm or deny the user's S-tier read on it at all. Recommend the Orchestrator add echoTap as a fourth MODE_PAIRS slot, or swap it in for tripwire on the armHalt/lock pair for one comparison run, before trusting any before/after number on this specific tone-down.

items.name: CHEAP SHOT
items.desc: Your first ATTACK each dive costs 0 RAM.
items.synergy: Pairs with the buffed JAM ANCHOR for a free opening freeze, and with REDIRECT's unlimited reach for a free first strike anywhere on the board.
items.counter: One-shot: only the very first ATTACK cast of the dive is free (the `econ.player.attacksCast === 0` gate in attackCost), so it buys one opening tempo swing, never a sustained discount; SCAN and DEFEND stay full price the whole dive.
items.engineNote: HOLD. No change this batch. Sits at the S ceiling per the user's tier list; existing hook (duel-actions.ts attackCost) is untouched. Revisit only after the halt-package sim (jamAnchor and tripwire buffs above) lands, since a free opening cast into a now-longer jam or a now-bigger tripwire burn could push this past S on its own, rather than the traps themselves needing a further nerf.

items.name: HALT DRIVER
items.desc: ATTACK config: plant halt traps. A sprung trap costs the intrusion its whole next turn.
items.synergy: TRIPWIRE (buffed above), the armHalt/lock MODE_PAIRS entry already in the kitted profile.
items.counter: PURGE (buffed SWEEP CREDIT now nets a real profit on a landed defuse), WARD DRIVER denies the plant outright.
items.engineNote: HOLD. No change this batch. Sits at the S ceiling alongside cfgLock per the user's tier list, and it is the mode TRIPWIRE rides. Simulate cfgArmHalt plus the tripwire and jamAnchor package as one unit before ever touching cfgArmHalt itself, since stacking a second buff on top of tripwire's own bump would double dip on the same read that made LOCK and HALT dominate pick rate per the story-retune-1 memory diagnosis.

items.name: CLAMP DRIVER
items.desc: DEFEND config: freeze junctions for 2 rounds against rotation and redirects.
items.synergy: LOCK_ROUNDS (shared, untouched); WARD DRIVER's now-symmetric duration is its nearest neighbor this batch, not a buff to LOCK itself.
items.counter: Unaffected by anything in this batch. REDIRECT's unlimited reach plus the buffed JAM ANCHOR freeze are the sharpest counters to a LOCK-only build baiting a rotation onto a locked node elsewhere.
items.engineNote: HOLD. No change this batch, and LOCK_ROUNDS (kit.ts, shared with the opponent) is explicitly off limits this cycle. Per the story-retune-1 memory note: LOCK was left flat last cycle specifically because it is an unconditional freeze with no fire condition, and PAR's rotation budget already makes forcing opponent reroutes more valuable without touching LOCK itself. This cycle's buffs (tripwire, jamAnchor, sweepCredit, cfgArmSiphon baseline) all target LOCK's competitors, not LOCK, so check the post-batch pick rate before ever nerfing it directly.
